cases.description: Videos of police, firefighters, soldiers, medics and other first responders actually doing their job.
cases.label: First responders on duty
cases.definition: Member only if the item text establishes both: (1) a central person is identified as a police officer (any branch, including auxiliary or court police), firefighter, soldier/armed police, doctor, nurse, paramedic or professional rescue worker; (2) the text describes them actively doing that job in the events shown (rescuing, treating, testing, questioning, arresting, mediating, escorting, investigating), or states that they are on duty in those events (e.g. 'on duty', 'responding to a call', 'flood relief'). Not members: they only issue a notice, statement or advice; are the victim or subject of a court case; appear off duty, in a skit, drama, dance or costume; or their role or duty is only implied.

cases.description: Stuff that happens overseas, or where the people in it are foreigners.
cases.label: Set abroad or about foreigners
cases.definition: Member only if the item text establishes either: (a) the scene or the reported event takes place in a named or explicitly foreign country (not mainland China, Hong Kong, Macao or Taiwan), or (b) the main people are explicitly identified as foreign nationals or foreigners ('laowai', 'foreigners', 'Americans', etc.). Not members: Chinese people or officials discussing foreign matters from China; Chinese places said to look like abroad; people who hold or regained Chinese nationality; Taiwan/Hong Kong residents; foreign brands or words without a stated foreign setting or person.

cases.description: Clips where you see someone or something before and after a makeover.
cases.label: Before-and-after transformation in the clip
cases.definition: Member only if the item text indicates the video itself shows the same person, animal, object or picture in a before state and an after state of a visible change in appearance or condition. Counts: outfit/makeup transformation clips (titles or hashtags such as 'outfit change', 'wardrobe change', 'transform', 'ultimate transformation'), makeup removal, photo restoration, side-by-side results. Not members: figurative turnarounds (career 'comeback', grades), behaviour comparisons (before vs after marriage, then vs now), policies about renovation, workouts promising future change, or merely wearing a costume.

cases.description: Videos shot in rainy, windy, or flood conditions.
cases.label: Scenes in rain, snow, storms or flood conditions.
cases.definition: Counts only if both are met: (1) the text indicates the video images or reported events occur in rain (of any intensity), snow, hail, typhoon or strong wind, or in flooding/ponding/standing water caused by such weather (including flood relief scenes); (2) that weather or its consequences actually appear in the video footage, not metaphor, jingles, weather knowledge, or slogans unrelated to the images. Not included: clear weather, high temperatures, rainbows, sunsets; slogan-style tags (like 'floods are ruthless but people are kind') without describing footage; post-event disputes about soaked cars; joking or metaphorical uses of weather (e.g. 'don’t worry when it rains').

cases.description: Videos that mention a specific amount of money, such as prices, wages, fines or compensation.
cases.label: Mentions a specific monetary amount.
cases.definition: Count it whenever the text explicitly contains a specific monetary amount: a number (Arabic numerals or Chinese numerals) plus a currency unit (yuan, kuai, ten thousand yuan, US dollars, ¥, etc.), indicating price, cost, income, salary, fine, compensation, reward, amount involved in a case, etc. Specific amounts used metaphorically or in a quotation also count. Do not count: instances that only say "money", "save money", or "owe how much money" without a specific amount; indeterminate expressions like "a few taels of silver"; cases where the character after a number like "kuai" or "wan" is not used as a currency (for example, "2 kuai chicken nuggets", or "35 wan" without a stated unit); other numbers such as jin (catty), years old, years, phone numbers, etc.

cases.description: Videos of ordinary laborers at work like food delivery riders, couriers, stall vendors or construction workers.
cases.label: Work scenes of grassroots laborers.
cases.definition: Counts only if both are met: (1) the text clearly identifies the video's main people as one of these workers: delivery riders, couriers, sanitation workers, construction/renovation/high-altitude workers, movers or porters, security guards, cleaners, restaurant servers, truck or taxi drivers, street vendors, and similar frontline manual or service workers; (2) the content relates to their work: actively working or delivering orders, at the workplace, work equipment or uniform, income or business conditions, not just a passing mention. Not included: using a profession as metaphor, joke, or flirtation; roleplay; talking only about delivery/courier policy or companies without specific workers; generic 'working a job' without a specific occupation; drivers who just happen to appear in a story.
